chapterTag.category: AP Calc BC BC-1 — Advanced Integration

body.en: Unit 6BC · Advanced Integration Techniques covers essential College Board AP Calculus BC competencies across foundational mechanics, intermediate analysis, and advanced FRQ problem solving.

blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Integration by Parts & Partial Fractions

body.en: Master the integration by parts formula \(\int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du\) (using the LIATE rule) and partial fraction decomposition for linear factors.
Integration by parts: \[ \int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du. \] LIATE priority: Logarithmic, Inverse trig, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential.

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

Evaluate the indefinite integral \(\int x\cos(x)\,dx\).

solution.en: Let \(u = x \implies du = dx\), and \(dv = \cos(x)\,dx \implies v = \sin(x)\). Applying parts: \[ \int x\cos(x)\,dx = x\sin(x) - \int \sin(x)\,dx = \mathbf{x\sin(x) + \cos(x) + C}. \]

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Tabular Integration & Partial Fractions with Distinct Factors

body.en: Accelerate repeated integration by parts with tabular integration, and integrate rational functions with distinct linear denominators.

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

Evaluate \(\int \frac{5x - 7}{x^2 - 3x + 2}\,dx\) using partial fraction decomposition.

solution.en: Factor denominator: \((x - 1)(x - 2)\). Set up: \[ \frac{5x - 7}{(x-1)(x-2)} = \frac{A}{x-1} + \frac{B}{x-2} \implies 5x - 7 = A(x-2) + B(x-1). \] For \(x = 1\): \(-2 = -A \implies A = 2\). For \(x = 2\): \(3 = B \implies B = 3\). Integrate: \[ \int \left(\frac{2}{x-1} + \frac{3}{x-2}\right)dx = \mathbf{2\ln|x-1| + 3\ln|x-2| + C}. \]

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced — Improper Integrals & Discontinuous Integrands

body.en: Evaluate improper integrals with infinite limits \(\int_a^\infty f(x)\,dx = \lim_{b\to\infty} \int_a^b f(x)\,dx\) and interior vertical asymptotes.

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

Evaluate the improper integral \(\int_0^1 \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx\) or state that it diverges.

solution.en: The integrand has an infinite discontinuity at the lower limit \(x = 0\). Rewrite as a limit: \[ \lim_{a \to 0^+} \int_a^1 x^{-1/2}\,dx = \lim_{a \to 0^+} \left[ 2\sqrt{x} \right]_a^1 = \lim_{a \to 0^+} (2\sqrt{1} - 2\sqrt{a}) = 2 - 0 = \mathbf{2}. \] The integral converges to 2.
